before: Students, faculty researchers, advisers, and research personnel need access that is appropriate to their responsibilities, so that progress can be seen clearly and each person remains accountable for their part in the work. A useful system must therefore distinguish editable drafts from submitted versions and retain decisions and recommendations. It should also show chapter progress without giving every user review authority.     Research metadata, supporting documents, publications, and intellectual-property records need consistent organization so that they can be found and managed with ease. These records also require appropriate access controls to protect them from unauthorized use. The study should therefore establish existing retrieval practices and measure representative retrieval tasks before claiming an improvement.RMS addresses these needs through browser-based interfaces, server-side processing, and relational data storage. Its implemented stack uses HTML, CSS, JavaScript, PHP, and MySQLi for database access. The project is developed locally using XAMPP. Centralized records and backend controls support the intended workflow; security, reliability, usability, and efficiency remain matters to evaluate through defined tasks and technical checks.
after: Student and faculty researchers need clear visibility into their research-title and chapter submissions, review decisions, and recommendations. Both follow the same submission workflow. The system distinguishes editable drafts from locked submissions, preserves submission history, and displays chapter progress. Administrators and research staff with the required permissions perform formal review and approval. before: Users  The platform uses four account roles—administrator, research staff, faculty, and student—with dedicated navigation and access controls. Access depends on the role, assigned action permissions, and the ownership or assignment rules of the relevant record:
after: Users  The platform accommodates four account roles: Administrator, Research Staff, Faculty, and Student. Faculty and students participate as researchers and follow the same title-and-chapter submission workflow. Administrators and research staff perform administrative and decision-making tasks according to their permissions. Access to individual records depends on the applicable role permissions, record ownership, and project membership.

before: Faculty  May submit and track their own research through the canonical title-and-chapter workflow. Assigned advisers may view and guide relevant student research where supported. Adviser assignment alone does not authorize formal title or chapter decisions.
after: Faculty  Creates and edits research-title drafts, submits titles for review, and submits Chapters 1–5 sequentially after title approval. Faculty researchers view decisions and recommendations, revise returned submissions, and resubmit their work through the same workflow used by student researchers. Submitted versions remain locked during review and after approval. Formal review and approval are performed by administrators and research staff with the required permissions.

before: Student  Creates and edits eligible research drafts, submits titles and sequential chapters, views decisions and recommendations, and revises returned work. Access to documents and associated records remains subject to the applicable backend rules.
after: Student  Creates and edits research-title drafts, submits titles for review, and submits Chapters 1–5 sequentially after title approval. Student researchers view decisions and recommendations, revise returned submissions, and resubmit their work through the same workflow used by faculty researchers. Submitted versions remain locked during review and after approval. Formal review and approval are performed by administrators and research staff with the required permissions.

before: Role-Based Access Control.  Restriction of application actions by account role, supplemented in RMS by explicit staff action permissions and relevant ownership or assignment checks.
after: Role-Based Access Control.  A mechanism that restricts application functions according to account roles and explicit action permissions. In RMS, faculty and students use the shared researcher workflow, while administrators and appropriately authorized research staff perform formal review and approval. Access to research records also follows the applicable ownership and project-membership rules.

before: Application Processing. PHP handles requests, authenticated sessions, permitted actions, validation, and document operations. Canonical title and chapter submission pages are shared by student and faculty researchers. The review helper separates administrator authority from research-staff permissions and records decisions against preserved submission versions.
after: Application Processing. PHP handles requests, authenticated sessions, permitted actions, validation, and document operations. Faculty and student researchers use the same title-and-chapter submission pages. Administrators and research staff with the required permissions review submitted versions and record decisions and recommendations. The application preserves submission history and enforces editing restrictions on submitted work.

before: Security. Check permitted and prohibited actions, record ownership or assignment, direct-route document access, CSRF handling, input validation, and submitted-version locks. Survey responses alone cannot establish security effectiveness.
after: Security. Verify that faculty and student researchers can perform permitted actions on eligible research records and cannot perform formal title or chapter review and approval. Check administrator and research-staff permissions, record ownership, project-membership access, direct-route document access, CSRF handling, input validation, and submitted-version locks. Respondent ratings alone cannot establish that these controls are effective.

before: Fourth, role-based access-control research supports separating authority from simple participation in a project. For RMS, faculty researcher or adviser access does not replace administrator/staff decision permissions. Security checks must include attempted actions outside the assigned authority.
after: Fourth, role-based access-control research supports a clear distinction between research submission and formal decision-making authority. Faculty and students use the same researcher workflow, while administrators and research staff with the required permissions perform title and chapter review and approval. Security verification must include attempts to access other researchers’ records, modify locked submissions, or perform decisions without authorization.

before: Application Processing.  PHP handles authorization, validation, uploads/downloads, locked submissions, version capture, and review decisions. Following the access-policy verification focus of Le et al. (2022), tests should compare implemented rights with intended permissions.
after: Application Processing.  PHP handles authorization, validation, document operations, submission locks, version capture, and review decisions. Faculty and students follow the same researcher workflow. Administrators and research staff exercise decision-making authority according to their permissions. Following the access-policy verification focus of Le et al. (2022), tests should compare implemented access rights with the intended permissions.
